title: Lemon Tart
subtitle: Classic French tarte au citron with a silky curd filling
excerpt: A crisp, sweet shortcrust pastry case filled with a smooth, intensely lemony curd of eggs, cream, and lemon juice. Sharp enough to make you blink, rich enough to keep eating.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tarte au citron is one of the great French dessert tarts, associated particularly with the cuisine of Nice and Provence where lemons are abundant. The filling is a lemon curd baked in the pastry case: the same mixture of eggs, sugar, cream, and lemon juice used for a cold curd but set by baking. The balance between sharp and sweet is the essence of the tart: a good lemon tart should be significantly sharp, the richness of the eggs and cream tempering rather than eliminating the acidity. The tart is served at room temperature, not cold: refrigerating dulls the flavour. A thin dusting of icing sugar, briefly blowtorched, is the classic French finish. The pastry case must be fully blind-baked before the filling goes in to prevent a soggy base.

content.text: The tart filling sets from the heat of the oven, but the exact setting point is narrow. The filling is done when it no longer jiggles in the centre when the tin is gently shaken and when the surface has a slight sheen without being liquid. If the oven is too hot, the eggs will scramble and the surface will crack. Bake at 160 C: lower is safer than higher. The tart firms further as it cools.

Line a 23 cm tart tin with the pastry. Trim and chill for 20 minutes. Blind-bake at 190 C with paper and beans for 15 minutes. Remove the beans and paper. Bake for a further 10 minutes until pale golden and completely dry. Reduce the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3.
Whisk together the eggs, yolks, and sugar until combined. Stir in the lemon juice, zest, and cream. Do not overmix. Pass through a fine sieve into a jug to remove the zest and any foam.

Pour the filling into the warm tart case. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 160 C until the edges are just set but the centre still has a gentle wobble. Cool completely in the tin. Dust with icing sugar before serving. Serve at room temperature.
